core.text: The stipulated 300 rpm trial stopped at second 60 and produced approximately 2.4 percent final-vial spread. This meets the bounded sample proxy once and counters universal necessity of sustained 900 rpm and stable optical checks. Repeatability and actual time savings remain unknown.

Higher commanded speed coincides with greater surface depression and fluctuating images; transient specks do not establish bubbles. Missing matched 900 rpm final samples prevent judging whether its optical fluctuations represent concentration gradients.

Proposed next action: use six fresh trials as three paired comparisons of commanded 300 and 900 rpm, each stirring for exactly 60 seconds without image-controlled restarts. Alternate speed order across pairs and depth-sampling order within pairs. Keep recipe, addition location, dye bottle, camera and reference procedure fixed. Log five-second images through second 120 and collect the specified depth samples then. Use the spill tray and stop on escaping liquid.

Report all raw vial readings, normalized spreads, stirring durations and target failures. Repeated 300 rpm success would support feasibility of the simpler fixed procedure under these conditions. Common-aliquot references assess repeatability, not calibration; equal planned stirring durations cannot establish comparative time savings.

residue.text: Even successful fixed-duration comparisons would not demonstrate that the optical rule actually prolongs stirring or that prolonged agitation renews disturbances. A later matched enabled-rule versus timer comparison would be needed; its outcomes remain hypothetical.
Commanded rpm lacks independent verification. Sampling may disturb gradients, and the final proxy describes sampled elevations after the quiet interval rather than uniformity throughout stirring.

Three paired comparisons provide limited replication. Bubble fraction and absolute concentration cannot be measured with these resources, and results do not establish performance for other liquids, vessels or continuous operation.

tension.account_a: Hypothesis: high-speed agitation produces transient image disturbances after sufficient mixing, so image spread can overstate remaining depth gradients.
tension.account_b: Rival hypothesis: image spread primarily reflects genuine residual depth gradients, and the lower-speed observed success is exceptional or sampling-mediated.
tension.prediction_a: In the proposed fixed-duration pairs, both speeds repeatedly meet final-vial spread at most 4 percent while 900 rpm has greater moving-image fluctuations that decline promptly after stopping.
tension.prediction_b: In those pairs, 300 rpm repeatedly exceeds 4 percent final-vial spread while 900 rpm meets the target; residual side spread persists after stopping and tracks final-vial failure. Mixed patterns leave these accounts unresolved, and cessation effects alone do not identify a mechanism.
